bull.b: Growing APHEXDA sales and royalties show increasing commercial adoption of the approved product. Continued uptake can provide a recurring revenue base while supporting development of BioLineRx’s broader oncology pipeline.

GLIX1’s blood-brain-barrier penetration, activity in resistant models and PARP-inhibitor synergy broaden its potential beyond a single indication. If clinical findings confirm the mechanism, the asset could address multiple underserved cancers.

Ongoing PDAC development and partner-led work in sickle cell disease create additional opportunities beyond APHEXDA’s current use. Retained rights in selected territories could preserve future milestone, royalty and commercialization upside.

bear.t: Persistent Losses and Negative Cash Flow
bear.b: The company remains dependent on external funding because commercialization has not yet produced self-sustaining cash generation. Persistent losses and negative free cash flow can constrain investment capacity and increase financing or dilution risk.

A runway extending only into H1 2027 leaves limited flexibility to fund clinical expansion, commercialization and corporate overhead. Unless cash generation improves, the company may need additional capital or partnerships to sustain its plans.

Reliance on a partner for commercialization reduces BioLineRx’s direct control over market coverage, sales execution and disclosure of operating metrics. This may make royalty growth less predictable and complicate planning for future revenue.
